_note: Plain-language summaries written by the SWIPES editor. A notice with an entry here becomes indexable (see scripts/story-pages.mjs). Kept separate from archive.json so the feed refresh never overwrites them.

summaries.6565bbc7797ee31a5e52: Saskatchewan has named the new hospital planned for Rosthern: it will be called Sask Valley Hospital, a name chosen to reflect the wider area it will serve.
summaries.852eb83ea8c2a52efd7a: Saskatchewan is buying a new PET/CT scanner for Royal University Hospital in Saskatoon. The machine combines two imaging tests in one scan and is used mainly to find and track cancer.
summaries.9e1665d216fb7c601dc7: Saskatchewan is putting $6.9 million toward 49 frontline police positions in Regina, aimed at faster response times and more officers on city streets.
summaries.5b7b13ddf663e975f64e: Saskatchewan says it is looking at bioenergy made from forestry by-products, both to give the forest industry new markets and to help meet future energy demand.
summaries.772fa6f353e19d14be90: Manitoba is setting up its first advisory table for commercial fishers, giving the industry a regular channel to advise the province on fishing policy.
summaries.eec9c6ac8435ee499eb5: X-ray services are back at the Dr. A. A. Wilkinson Memorial Health Centre in Old Perlican, Newfoundland and Labrador, after a new digital X-ray machine was installed. The centre is marking its 25th anniversary.
summaries.afc9c07deb28c400cb08: Newfoundland and Labrador Finance Minister Craig Pardy will present the province's 2026 Fall Economic and Fiscal Update on Monday, November 23, at the Confederation Building in St. John's.
summaries.11aef7abbe07f4f03147: Newfoundland and Labrador Justice Minister Helen Conway Ottenheimer will speak to media on Monday, November 23, about the province's Safer Communities and Neighbourhoods legislation.
summaries.c6a82af74f11946b2a26: Newfoundland and Labrador has started issuing the second payments under its Home Heating Supplement Program for households that heat with furnace or stove oil.
summaries.33d3b126118354d502d8: Newfoundland and Labrador has approved the offshore regulator's decision on the development plan for the Bay du Nord oil project, a key step before the project can move ahead.
summaries.f4fa2f53577f7c317ffe: On National Child Day (November 20), Prince Edward Island launched "Don't Wait, Make the Call", a campaign urging Islanders to report concerns about a child's safety.
summaries.ea2df4aecad17948720f: Alberta has updated its parent toolkit, which collects learning-at-home resources for families of students from kindergarten to Grade 9 in one place.
summaries.1c18eeb96cdfdde9f118: Alberta is giving $1.7 million to 13 projects that help wood manufacturers create new value-added products and diversify the province's forest industry.
summaries.5c3b312fe70897f6d9f5: Alberta has signed a partnership with Discover Airlines to strengthen direct flights between Alberta and Germany and bring more international visitors to the province.
summaries.f0b40374030f9c695f32: Alberta is investing $250 million to build thousands of affordable homes across the province.
summaries.30113316d07b43cf4e77: A fibre internet expansion by EH!tel is now complete in Bruce and Grey counties, Ontario, giving thousands of rural residents access to high-speed internet.
summaries.4dcf0a8ab98d07525bd2: Ontario is moving ahead with widening Highway 17 between Arnprior and Renfrew to improve safety, cut congestion and support a key trade route in Eastern Ontario.
summaries.74b39c0251f82984ac84: Construction has started on the redeveloped Banwell Gardens Care Centre in Windsor, Ontario. The long-term care home will have 192 modern beds, and the province expects about 650 jobs.
summaries.f17f042e0d0945bf7ec5: Ford of Canada is investing nearly $5 billion in Ontario, including a new production line for F-Series Super Duty trucks and new stamping capacity. Ford employs about 7,000 people in Canada, more than 2,000 of them in Oakville.
summaries.47bb7a468b44daf2cb99: Ontario and the federal government are investing $250 million in a new port facility in Sault Ste. Marie, meant to boost trade within Canada and with other countries and support growth in Northern Ontario.
summaries.3ba01046833ae6c42e03: The Ontario Parks Store has launched a winter collection of Canadian-made gear and gifts. All proceeds go to trail improvements, accessibility and visitor experiences in provincial parks.
summaries.fe5ba54ec56a5589b68c: British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson has sworn in a new cabinet, saying its focus is restoring confidence in government and building a stronger province.
